learning_from.description: The learner's explanation/best language. Every canonical learn-from language may participate when its localized bridge copy exists.

learning_language_full.description: Tier 1 and Tier 2 target languages with researched family-member distinctions, representative terms, cultural cautions, examples, and practice-ready relation features.

learning_language_game.description: All canonical learn-from languages have a core family vocabulary route for reusable Games. Tier 1 and Tier 2 use their rich target profiles; Tier 3 uses the smaller recognition-safe game vocabulary shard.

learning_language_comparison.description: Tier 3 may participate as a game/comparison target without implying a full grammar or culture curriculum path. Rich culture/usage explanations remain Tier 1 and Tier 2 until separately researched.

runtime_model.source_first: Show the localized source bridge in the learner's best available language before teaching the target system.
runtime_model.target_second_full: For Tier 1 and Tier 2, resolve the structured target profile and render the explanation, term set, distinctions, cultural note, examples, and safe practice.
runtime_model.target_second_tier3: For Tier 3, expose the core term set to Games/comparison surfaces only. Do not synthesize a rich cultural profile from the small vocabulary row.
runtime_model.pair_scaling: Never author a source-by-target matrix. Source copy, target profiles, and game terms are independent assets joined through stable relationship concepts.
runtime_model.fallback: If a source localization is below the user's trust threshold, use the normal best-language fallback. If a target lacks a rich profile, use the Tier 3 game path rather than inventing target prose.
